label: D1-only: fires after switching from a1 (S1 unrewarded) to a2 reaching S2.
terms: (phase == D1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (tv("action", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("state", -3) == 1) * (tv("reward", -3) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("action", -2) == 1) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("state", -2) == 2) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * prev_reward ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("action", -2) == -9)
explanation: Sparse feature (nonzero on 1.8% of steps), active only at D1. Its magnitude depends on the last two trials: it is largest when the trial before last was a1 / S1 and unrewarded and the last trial was a2 reaching S2, i.e. right after switching away from an unrewarded S1 to S2. The a1-then-a2 choice switch is the strongest single term, and S1-unrewarded two trials back adds to it. The free fit gets most of its gain from the four-factor conjunction (S1 unrewarded two back AND S2 last, at D1), which the short form cannot express because it allows at most three factors per term, so the short form only approximates it with pairwise terms. Belief, the trial three back and last-trial reward add little. Many large activations fall on the first trial of a window, where the history that drives it is not visible, which caps the score.
